name: NEPTUNE
aliases: Solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS fixed-dose combination
question: Does fixed-dose solifenacin plus tamsulosin OCAS improve storage and voiding symptoms more than tamsulosin OCAS or placebo in men with lower urinary tract symptoms?

arms.label: Solifenacin 6 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg daily
solifenacin 9 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg daily

design.population: 1,334 men aged at least 45 years with at least three months of storage and voiding lower urinary tract symptoms, total IPSS at least 13, maximum flow 4–12 mL/s, at least two severe urgency episodes and eight micturitions daily, estimated prostate weight under 75 g, and postvoid residual at most 150 mL.
design.locator: Full text, Methods sections 2.1–2.2, p 1004; Fig. 1, p 1005

verdictNote: The 6 mg combination met both coprimary endpoints; the 9 mg combination did not.
takeaway: Over 12 weeks, solifenacin 6 mg plus tamsulosin OCAS met prespecified IPSS superiority versus placebo, IPSS noninferiority versus tamsulosin, and TUFS superiority versus tamsulosin. The 9 mg combination failed IPSS noninferiority after multiplicity adjustment and TUFS superiority versus tamsulosin.

reports.label: Primary 12-week randomized report
reports.citation: van Kerrebroeck P, Chapple C, Drogendijk T, et al. "Combination Therapy with Solifenacin and Tamsulosin Oral Controlled Absorption System in a Single Tablet for Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms in Men: Efficacy and Safety Results from the Randomised Controlled NEPTUNE Trial." *Eur Urol.* 2013;64(6):1003-1012. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2013.07.034

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in total IPSS at 12 weeks (full analysis set); superiority versus placebo and noninferiority versus tamsulosin in both full-analysis and per-protocol sets

effect.p: <0.001 superiority versus placebo; 0.001 noninferiority versus tamsulosin

results.note: The −0.8-point difference versus tamsulosin is calculated from rounded adjusted arm changes, not a reported contrast estimate. Noninferiority margin 0.5; per-protocol results were consistent. No contrast confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods section 2.5, pp 1005–1006; Results section 3.2.1 and Fig. 2, p 1006; Table 2, p 1007

results.endpoint: Total Urgency and Frequency Score, 6 mg combination
results.measure: Adjusted mean change in TUFS at 12 weeks (full analysis set); superiority versus tamsulosin
results.note: The −1.4-point difference versus tamsulosin is calculated from rounded adjusted arm changes, not a reported contrast estimate. No contrast confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results section 3.2.1 and Fig. 2, p 1006; Table 2, p 1007

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in total IPSS at 12 weeks (full analysis set); superiority versus placebo and noninferiority versus tamsulosin in both full-analysis and per-protocol sets

effect.p: 0.006 superiority versus placebo; 0.028 nominal versus tamsulosin, not significant after multiplicity adjustment

results.note: The −0.3-point difference versus tamsulosin is calculated from rounded adjusted arm changes, not a reported contrast estimate. Noninferiority was not established after multiplicity adjustment. No contrast confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods section 2.5, pp 1005–1006; Results section 3.2.1 and Fig. 2, p 1006; Table 2, p 1007

results.endpoint: Total Urgency and Frequency Score, 9 mg combination
results.measure: Adjusted mean change in TUFS at 12 weeks (full analysis set); superiority versus tamsulosin
results.note: The −0.9-point difference versus tamsulosin is calculated from rounded adjusted arm changes, not a reported contrast estimate. No contrast confidence interval reported.
results.locator: Full text, Results section 3.2.1 and Fig. 2, p 1006; Table 2, p 1007

harms.label: Any and serious treatment-emergent adverse events
Drug-related dry mouth and constipation
harms.note: Safety population; investigators judged these adverse events drug-related.

harms.label: Catheter-requiring acute urinary retention
harms.locator: Full text, Results section 3.3, p 1008; Table 4, pp 1009–1010
harms.note: Safety population; five cases after randomization required catheterization. Table 4 lists drug-related events; the 6 mg case was not considered drug-related.

delivery.label: Randomized regimen
delivery.value: After a two-week placebo run-in, once-daily matching placebo, tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg, or a single fixed-dose tablet combining tamsulosin OCAS 0.4 mg with solifenacin 6 or 9 mg was given for 12 weeks; visits occurred at weeks 4, 8, and 12.

delivery.label: Randomized treatment completion
delivery.note: Completed treatment among safety-population participants; percentages as printed in Fig. 1.
